sources.facts: HeapSize takes the owning heap, flags and an actual allocation pointer, and returns SIZE_T. Its failure sentinel is SIZE_T(-1). It does not establish an extended error through SetLastError. A block from a different heap is outside defined behavior, so guest alias validation must precede the native call. The independently captured native result supplies capacity; the bridge does not substitute a requested-size calculation.

HeapReAlloc takes the same heap and a pointer returned by its earlier allocation or reallocation. With flags zero it can move. Success preserves the old content and returns at least the requested size; NULL preserves the original allocation. On x64 the returned allocation alignment is 16 bytes. The function does not establish extended error through SetLastError. Private pointer ownership must immediately follow a successful return, including any later observer or guest transport fault.
